record.reason: The primary source defines Router Prior Bias as a training-time bias that anchors router logits to a prior from a frozen base router while leaving the router trainable (abstract and §3). The paper compares post-training objectives on Moonlight-16B-A3B and Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base; its results are downstream task accuracy and routing retention, not inference latency, memory, or compute savings (§4-5). The evaluation removes the training-time prior hook and probes in inference mode to measure the trained router; inference mode is an evaluation protocol, not an inference-efficiency method.
record.title: Router Prior Bias: Preserving Base Routing Structure in MoE Post-Training
